Change c0469. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. VI; 1831 Ch. XXIII.

Context before (unchanged): The story is too connected to be mistaken for a dream, and I have no motive for falsehood."

1818 text: My manner, as I thus addressed him, was impressive, but calm; I had formed in my own heart a resolution to pursue my destroyer to death; and this purpose quieted my agony, and provisionally reconciled me to life. I now related my history briefly, but with firmness and precision, marking the dates with accuracy, and never deviating into invective or exclamation.

1831 text: My manner, as I thus addressed him, was impressive, but calm; I had formed in my own heart a resolution to pursue my destroyer to death; and this purpose quieted my agony, and for an interval reconciled me to life. I now related my history, briefly, but with firmness and precision, marking the dates with accuracy, and never deviating into invective or exclamation.

Diff: My manner, as I thus addressed him, was impressive, but calm; I had formed in my own heart a resolution to pursue my destroyer to death; and this purpose quieted my agony, and [-provisionally-] {+for an interval+} reconciled me to life. I now related my history {+,+} briefly, but with firmness and precision, marking the dates with accuracy, and never deviating into invective or exclamation.

Context after (unchanged): The magistrate appeared at first perfectly incredulous, but as I continued he became more attentive and interested; I saw him sometimes shudder with horror, at others a lively surprise, unmingled with disbelief, was painted on his countenance.

result.rationale: "provisionally reconciled" becomes "for an interval reconciled": both mark the resolution as temporary, so the meaning is largely kept, though the adverb's sense of conditional acceptance is replaced by a plainly temporal phrase. The added comma after "history" is trivial.
